ROW.COLUMN: Increasingly, fraud is being perpetrated by organized crime rings who leverage increasingly sophisticated fraud techniques and advanced technology methods to gain access to significant numbers of customer accounts. Many of these rings are based overseas. The subsequent movement of funds, both within and outside of the institution, can become quite complicated as the fraudsters attempt to hide their tracks and make potential recovery impossible by moving defrauded funds offshore. A sudden change in transaction activity involving offshore transfers, especially those to high risk geographies, may be suspicious and warrant additional investigation. This scenario monitors transaction activity and detects significant changes from the typical activity of an account which could be indicative of potential fraudulent behavior, such as payments fraud or account takeover. It identifies accounts that may be considered to be at risk by monitoring for electronic funds transfers, check, and monetary instrument activity involving high risk geographies and detecting significant changes from the previous monthly high-risk geography transaction activity.
See TSD for complete scenario description.
